title: Cognition in Depression
summary: Impairments in cognition, i.e. attention, memory, planning and decision making, are frequently observed in people with depression. In this study a particular aspect of cognition will be examined in depression, the so-called proactive control. Proactive control refers to the ability to direct attention to expected events in order to anticipate these such that they can be optimally responded to. There are findings in the literature which suggest that this ability is impaired in people with depression. In this study, this ability will be examined more closely in an experiment on eye movements. One aim is to examine the neural correlates, i.e. the accompanying brain processes. It will also be examined whether the extent of impairment in proactive control is associated with affective, i.e. emotion-related features. To do so, patients with depression and healthy controls will be invited to a study in which they perform a task that requires responses to pictures of faces displaying different emotions. During task performance, different methods will be applied to measure brain activity; functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) in Bonn and electroencephalography (EEG) in Tirol. Overall, we expect to obtain a better understanding of cognition and underlying brain function in depression as well as the role of affect.
conditions: DSM-5: 296.31, 296.32, 296.33 (diagnosis of depression according to DSM-5

interventions.name: At each site (Bonn, Tirol), a group of 50 patients with depression as well as a group of 50 healthy controls will be studied. There is no treatment or other intervention as part of this study.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients:
• Diagnosis of depression (DSM-5 categories 296.21, 296.22, 296.23, 296.31, 296.32, 296.33)
• 18-45 years old,
• right-handed,
• normal or with contact lenses corrected eyesight

Controls:
• healthy,
• 18-45 years old,
• right-handed,
• normal or with contact lenses corrected eyesight
Exclusion criteria:
Patients:
• Aged below 18 or above 45 years,
• Current physical disease,
• Current neurological disease especially ataxias,
• Past diagnosis of neurological disorders,
• Eye injuries or diseases,
• Wearing glasses,
• Current participation in a medicines trial,
• Claustrophobia, or having had a panic attack in an enclosed space in the past,
• Metal parts in the body or hair (earrings, piercings),
• large tattoos in upper part of the body,
• metallic implants, protheses, pacemakers or medication pumps (e.g. insulin pumps),
• for women: IUD,
• having done welding work in the past,
• wearing glasses (contact lenses are no problem),
• current or past hearing deficits,
• having ever had operations on the heart, eyes or head

Controls:
• Aged below 18 or above 45 years,
• Current physical disease,
• Current psychiatric disease
• Current neurological disease especially ataxias,
• Past diagnosis of neurological or psychiatric disorders,
• Eye injuries or diseases,
• Wearing glasses,
• Current participation in a medicines trial,
• Claustrophobia, or having had a panic attack in an enclosed space in the past,
• Metal parts in the body or hair (earrings, piercings),
• large tattoos in upper part of the body,
• metallic implants, protheses, pacemakers or medication pumps (e.g. insulin pumps),
• for women: IUD,
• having done welding work in the past,
• wearing glasses (contact lenses are no problem),
• current or past hearing deficits,
• having ever had operations on the heart, eyes or head
